NASTUDIONetwork Assignment Studio

Designed by Johan Irvenå — with the machines handling the minor details.

Network Assignment Studio is a local-first browser tool for building road-network models and assigning travel demand to them. Draw zones, junctions (including roundabouts) and directed links on a map, enter or import O-D matrices, and calculate route assignments with All-or-Nothing (AON), Incremental loading or user-equilibrium Method of Successive Averages (UE/MSA). Compare scenarios (network edits, toll schemes, signal plans) and saved runs, calibrate O-D demand against observed link, turn, screenline and zone counts, and inspect flows with select-link analysis, turning movements and Sankey diagrams.

NAS calculates the assignments itself. TomTom O/D Analysis results — flow matrices, trip statistics and Selected Link volumes — are external observations retrieved with your own API key; NAS shows them as supplied, and a TomTom flow matrix holds normalized shares that must be scaled to absolute demand before it can be assigned. NAS is a static, macroscopic assignment model: it does not simulate individual vehicles or queue dynamics.

Built with
  • Leaflet 1.9.4 — interactive map (BSD-2-Clause; embedded)
  • MapLibre GL JS 5.24.0 — vector basemap renderer (BSD-3-Clause; embedded, evaluated only when a vector basemap is selected)
  • MapLibre GL Leaflet 0.1.4 — Leaflet binding for MapLibre (ISC; embedded)
  • IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Serif and Azeret Mono typefaces (SIL OFL 1.1; embedded)

Optional services, contacted only after an explicit action:

  • Basemaps — OpenFreeMap vector styles (tiles.openfreemap.org; © OpenMapTiles, data © OpenStreetMap contributors) and Esri Satellite / Topographic legacy no-token tiles (server.arcgisonline.com), after a one-time consent. Presentation only.
  • OSRM — public demo router (router.project-osrm.org) for road snapping and link geometry; it receives only the clicked or endpoint coordinates.
  • TomTom O/D Analysis API (api.tomtom.com) — analysis creation, results and trip statistics with your session API key, subject to TomTom’s terms of service.

Conventions
  • Right-hand traffic: a two-way road is a pair of directed links; flow stripes and lane markings sit right of the centreline in the travel direction.
  • Units: lengths in metres, speeds in km/h, capacity in vehicles per hour for the whole directed link, demand and assigned volumes in trips of the active matrix’s period.
  • Routes minimise generalized cost in seconds — free-flow time × link cost factor, plus junction and turn penalties, signal delay and tolls × toll weight — with one turn-restriction-aware shortest-path engine shared by AON, Incremental and UE (MSA). Incremental and UE (MSA) update link times with the BPR function; timed signal movements use Webster delay.
  • V/C and BPR congestion compare assigned volume with hourly capacity, so they are meaningful when the matrix represents one hour of demand. Thresholds in the v/c colouring are 0.85 and 1.00.
  • Map coordinates are WGS84 longitude/latitude; zone import also accepts SWEREF99 TM.
  • Negative O-D cells (difference matrices) are skipped by assignment with a warning.
Data & network

Opening this file performs no network request: the application code, map libraries and fonts are embedded. Requests happen only for the optional services above, each restricted to its registered HTTPS origin and paths; anything else is blocked before sending, and a failed service never breaks local editing or analysis. Project labels, demand and results are never sent to the basemap or routing providers. TomTom API keys are kept for the browser session only — never in project files, browser storage or exports. Palette, layer and panel choices are browser preferences, not project data.

v2 limits: LineString ≤ 2 km · Polygon ≤ 3 km². A two-way street offers both directions in the selector; MultiPolygon zones cannot be used (the API takes one Polygon).

LineString 5–50 km · Polygon 5–10 km
The TomTom Orbis map used for map matching — distinct from the visual basemap. With VOLUME ticked, TomTom's single volume map for the requested calendar year is required and locked. VOLUME is a modeled estimate: it needs volume coverage on every requested date and a last date at least four days in the past. For a LineString it also requires the TomTom road-segment probe (exactly ONE Orbis segment); polygons may request VOLUME — TomTom decides entrance/exit coverage.
Time definition
Uses the Dates & Times defined on the Origin/Destination tab (shared v2 rules: one-hour minimum ranges; each date × time combination becomes one independently normalized result slice).
